blocks.x: On Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television shows, and more. This time, we ask: where was The Diplomat filmed? This story contains major spoilers for season four.

Watching The Diplomat is like being a fly on the wall in some of the world’s most powerful rooms and buildings. But the Netflix series, though often immensely dramatic, rarely puts its characters in places that reflect them intimately. Instead, as production designer Curt Beech explains, The Diplomat is about “bringing the characters together physically but never emotionally in spaces the public don’t get to see.”

“The places may be historical, but they're almost never personal,” he says. “That is what's so different about this show from a design standpoint. Usually, we're creating someone's bedroom or their house, and we dig into their family history and who they are and what they like. We don't get any of that here because the spaces that they inhabit are not theirs. They are almost always visitors.”

The fourth season of The Diplomat opens with a bang—literally. In the first episode, US President Grace Penn, played by Allison Janney, survives an assassination attempt outside Windsor Castle. She becomes increasingly unpredictable afterwards, confusing her husband Todd (Bradley Whitford), Vice President Hal Wyler (Rufus Sewell), and Kate Wyler, the US ambassador to the UK (Keri Russell). The story brings the characters from Windsor Castle to Washington, DC to Lucca, Italy, where it concludes on a cliffhanger at a meeting of the G7.

Beech used some of the same locations and sets from past seasons, but also brought new locations to life in England, New York, and Italy. The interior sets were created at Steiner Studios in New York, while Wrotham House returned as Winfield House, the residence of the United States ambassador in London. Here Beech breaks down the key locations from The Diplomat Season 4.

Season 4 opens with an impromptu visit to Windsor Castle. As the envoy leaves the British royal residence to fly back to the US, President Penn gets shot by an unknown assailant. Beech combined nine different locations to create Windsor Castle and its grounds. The exterior and inner courtyard were filmed at Burghley House, while Belvoir Castle, Lancaster House and the British Foreign Office were used for interiors. Back in the US, the team filmed at Woolworth Estate, St. Josaphat Monastery Library and Sleepy Hollow Country Club. The grandiose panic room where Kate and Hal are locked down after the shooting was filmed in the crypt of a church on the Upper West Side.

“It's a lot of different architectural styles, but that is typical of these houses,” Beech says. “Windsor has a bunch of things going on because these houses are very, very old, and they've been built during different centuries with different people in charge of the construction. We embraced that. We also have a mix of things that are accurate to Windsor Castle and things that aren’t.”

After she is shot, President Penn is airlifted in Marine One to a docked United States aircraft carrier for surgery. Beech used the parking lot at Steiner Studios for the helicopter landing, while a Marine training facility in New York City was transformed into the interiors.

“We did real takeoffs and landings with the helicopter,” Beech says. “While it was on the ground, we dressed the interior because Marine One feels like a private jet inside. It's very luxurious and well appointed. But you can’t add weight to a helicopter like that without going through a lot of different FAA approvals, so we couldn’t keep it dressed while flying.”
